standard: SAT Standard English Conventions: modifier placement (dangling and misplaced modifiers). Aligned to CCSS L.9-10.1 and L.11-12.1.
source: Original content written for Pip (no third-party text copied).
attribution: Pip team, original. Common Core standards are cited for alignment only.
in_scope: an opening phrase before a comma and the noun right after the comma
fixing a dangling modifier by moving the doer right after the comma
checking a new sentence for who or what the opening phrase is about
captions and group-chat replies as pictures of a modifier stuck on the wrong thing
out_of_scope: modifiers at the end of a sentence (next mission)

look_fors: Says the phrase before the comma describes the noun that comes right after the comma
Says that is why 'my backpack' ends up being the one running (the sentence thinks the next noun is the doer)
May use a caption on the wrong photo or a reply to the wrong message
probe_ladder: why is that wrong? 'running to the bus, my backpack fell open' sounds fine to me.
so in that sentence, who is running to the bus?
what word comes right after the comma, and what does the sentence say it did?
then 'covered in sprinkles, my sister ate the donut' is fine, because everyone knows who i mean. that's what my rule says.
concrete: what if i read 'running to the bus, my backpack fell open' slowly out loud, who is running?
connections: so it's like a caption stuck on the wrong photo?
so it's like replying to the wrong message in a group chat?
concepts.friend_nudge: My friend said a caption under the wrong photo makes the photo say something silly…? I'm not sure how that helps.
concepts.aha: ohh so the sentence thinks the backpack is the one running.

look_fors: Puts the one doing the action right after the comma (for example 'Running to the bus, I ...')
Keeps the opening phrase and rewrites the rest of the sentence
Says it works because now the next noun is the runner
probe_ladder: how would you fix 'running to the bus, my backpack fell open'?
i'll try: 'running to the bus, the bus was late.' is that fixed?
what would you put next to the comma so the runner is the one running?
then 'running to the bus, my backpack fell open' is fine if i say it fast. that's what my rule says.
concrete: what if i keep 'running to the bus,' and then write the person who is running?
connections: so it's like tagging the right person in the photo?
concepts.friend_nudge: Someone in my class said you just start the second part with whoever did it…? I don't know what that does for the backpack.
concepts.aha: ok so I goes right after the comma and the backpack stops running.

look_fors: Checks a new sentence by asking who or what the opening phrase is about
Notices that 'Covered in sprinkles, my sister ...' says the sister is covered in sprinkles
Fixes it by moving the right noun (the donut) next to the comma, or rewriting
probe_ladder: is 'covered in sprinkles, my sister ate the donut' ok?
i'll guess it's fine because it has a comma after the phrase. am i right?
what would you ask yourself to check a sentence like that?
then 'walking the dog, the leash broke' is fine, since leashes can be walking. that's what my rule says.
concrete: what if i try 'covered in sprinkles, my sister ate the donut' on a friend, who do they picture covered?
connections: so it's like checking who a caption is really under before you laugh?
concepts.friend_nudge: My cousin said to point at the first noun after the comma and ask if it fits the phrase…? I'm not sure that is it.
concepts.aha: ok so I point at the noun after the comma and ask if it fits.

quiz.line: The backpack, because it's the noun right after the comma. So it was running.

quiz.pip_answer: Running to the bus, I felt my backpack fall open.
quiz.line: Running to the bus, I felt my backpack fall open. The I goes next to the comma.
Your rule: just check there's a comma after the phrase. There is one. So it's fine, my sister is covered in sprinkles and that's fine. Following your rule anyway. 😵

retry.pip_answer: No, the sister is the one covered.
retry.line: A comma isn't enough. Who's covered in sprinkles? The donut. So my sister ate it covered, which is wrong.

ko_strike.right: the phrase describes the next noun
